To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Pure” versus co- occurring externalizing and internalizing symptoms in childhood may be influenced by failure to achieve relevant socio-developmental markers, which paradoxically prevent the emergence of co-occurrent symptoms for some children.

failure to attain specific socio-developmental milestones may explain why some children do not develop heterotypically related internalizing and externalization symptoms, but that other children may develop heterotypic symptoms due to the attainment of relevant socio-developmental markers.
failure to attain socio-development milestones may prevent the development co-occurring heterotypic symptoms for some children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why some children show pure versus co-occurrent internalizing and externalising problems.
understanding why some children with internalizing symptoms do not also show concurrent externalizing symptoms and vice versa.
the development and validation of an integrative, socio-developmental model of internalizing and externalising symptoms in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

children who do not attain relevant socio-develop mental milestones (e.g., lack of peer relations) are less likely to develop co-occurring externalizing/internalizing symptoms than are children who do not fail to attain relevant socio- developmental milestones (e.g. peer relations).

the failure to attain relevant social and emotional milestones may be a protective factor that prevents the development of co-existing internalizing and externalising symptoms in a subset of children.

the failure to attain relevant developmental milestones (i.e. peer relations for anxious, self-evaluation for impulsive) may prevent subgroups from developing co-occuring, heterotypic internalizing and externalising symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

children with high social anxiety, high withdrawal and inhibition, high impulsivity, high hyperactivity, and high emotional reactivity may have difficulty attaining socio-developal milestones and, in turn, be less likely to show co-occurring heterotypic symptoms.
failure to reach certain socio-developmental milestones may prevent the emergence of co-occurrent symptoms in children.
the failure to attain certain socio-developmental milestones may prevent the development and expression of co-occurrent internalizing and externalising disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children with co-occurring externalizing and internalizing symptoms may have a more severe form of the same disorder, rather than a different disorder.
failure to attain socio-development milestones may explain why some children do not show co-occurring heterotypic symptoms.
the failure to attain relevant milestones may explain why some children with pure internalizing and/or externalizing symptoms do not show co-occurring heterotypic symptoms.
